lesson_title: From a Balloon to a Lightning Bolt
hook_text: The spark from a door handle and a lightning bolt are the same thing. One is just a lot bigger.
clip_script: Rub a balloon on your hair and your hair rises to meet it. Rubbing scraped tiny negative particles called electrons off your hair and onto the balloon. The balloon is now negative, your hair positive, and opposite charges attract. Each hair is positive like its neighbours, so they push apart and stand up. Like charges repel, unlike charges attract. Now scale it up. In a towering thundercloud, ice and water crash together and swap charge until the bottom of the cloud is hugely negative. When the difference gets big enough, charge leaps to the ground: lightning, heating the air to about 30 000 degrees. The air bursts outwards with a crack of thunder. Count the seconds from flash to bang and divide by three for the distance in kilometres. The Highveld gets some of the most lightning on Earth. When thunder roars, go indoors.
visual_style: Close-up of hair lifting toward a balloon; animated electrons hopping across; a time-lapse Highveld thunderstorm; a lightning strike in slow motion; a countdown timer from flash to thunder.
mood: Playful turning dramatic, ending on safety.
pacing: Light opening trick, rising drama in the storm, a firm safety finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and learn the lightning safety rules.
